## Introduction

One of the biological applications we've seen before is transcriptomics (or RNA-Seq data). Let's see if we can use the 'RNASeq123' package to do some analysis 


```{r Bioc123}

# Normally, we would check to see if BiocManager is available. If not, install it.
# We avoid reinstalling packages during a render so the Rmd stays reproducible.
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("BiocManager")
}

# Install optional organism mapping packages only when needed; do not fail the
# render if the package is unavailable in this environment.
if (!requireNamespace("Mus.musculus", quietly = TRUE)) {
  message("Mus.musculus is not available; the gene-name mapping section will be skipped.")
}

```

## The RNAseq123 Vignette

Vignettes are like the --help or man pages in bash, but MUCH nicer and typically more helpful. 

If a vignette exists for a package, you can view it (in a web browser) using the browseVignettes() function with the package name, like below.  

```{r 123Vignette}
#library(RNAseq123)
#browseVignettes("RNAseq123")
```

After you install the packages, you'll still need to load the libraries to use them. 

```{r ExploreLibs}

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(limma)
  # library(Glimma)
  library(edgeR)
  if (requireNamespace("Mus.musculus", quietly = TRUE)) {
    library(Mus.musculus)
  } else {
    message("Mus.musculus is unavailable; gene mapping examples will be skipped.")
  }
})
#files <- ("GPL6887_MouseWG-6_V2_0_R3_11278593_A.txt")
#read.delim(files[1], nrow=20)
# Loading the libraries might force other library dependencies to be loaded
# (just like for the install).
#tail(read.delim(files[1])

gset <- GEOquery::getGEO("GSE57465", GSEMatrix = TRUE, getGPL = FALSE)
if (length(gset) > 1) idx <- grep("GPL6887", attr(gset, "names")) else idx <- 1
gset <- gset[[idx]]
expression <- Biobase::exprs(gset)
head(expression[, c(1, 3), drop = FALSE])
```
